summary: Tested new banner feature: 4:1 aspect ratio crop + fixed-palette color swatches (bg color fallback + heading color) for Skægagamer app. Backend PUT/GET /api/admin/settings verified via curl: colors persist correctly, null resets work, image removal + bg color fallback works. Frontend Playwright testing on mobile viewport (375x667) confirmed: Admin banner section renders with 4:1 wide preview box (not tall), color swatches (1 none + 10 colors) render and are tappable for both bg-color and heading-color rows with checkmark highlight on selection, live preview updates, 'Gem banner' save succeeds with 'Banner gemt' toast, and settings persist after reload. PageBanner component correctly shows solid-color fallback banner (previously hidden when no image) with correct heading text color (verified computed CSS color rgb(61,64,91) = #3D405B matches saved heading_color) across Overview, Ugeplaner (Schedule), and Opgaver (Tasks) tabs. Backend regression test suite ran 15 tests: 13 passed, 2 failed due to leftover test data pollution from prior iteration (duplicate time '07:00'/'20:00' already exist in DB from previous test runs) - NOT a real app bug, confirmed via curl that times collection already contains these values from earlier sessions.

minor.issue: No issues found - banner_bg_color and heading_color fields save/retrieve correctly, exclude_unset partial update works as expected, null values correctly reset fields.

action_items: Test data pollution in TestScheduleSlotsAndOverview: times '07:00' and '20:00' already exist in DB from earlier iterations, causing duplicate-time 400 errors in test_full_flow_schedule_and_overview and test_update_schedule_slot. Recommend either using unique/randomized time values in tests or adding proper cleanup/idempotent seed handling. Not a banner-feature regression; pre-existing test data issue.
No action items for the banner feature itself - implementation verified working correctly end-to-end (backend persistence + frontend UI + PageBanner fallback rendering).
critical_code_review_comments: admin.tsx and PageBanner.tsx are clean, correctly reuse SWATCH_COLORS constant, proper testID coverage on all interactive elements (swatches, save/remove buttons, text input).
PageBanner correctly implements 3-way fallback logic: image+overlay text -> solid bg-color+centered text -> null (hidden) when nothing set - matches requested behavior.
Checkmark icon color correctly adapts (dark on white swatch, white otherwise) for contrast readability.
No backend changes needed as models/routes already supported these fields - confirmed correct via testing.
Minor observation: previous testing agent reported blank screenshots for admin screen; this was NOT reproduced - admin screen renders correctly in this session across multiple screenshot captures.

success_rate.backend: 13/15 (2 failures are pre-existing test-data pollution unrelated to banner feature)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of banner feature flows tested passed

seed_data_creation: Modified app_settings singleton via curl/UI during testing: final state has banner_bg_color='#81B29A', heading_color='#3D405B', banner_text='Skægagamer Test Banner', banner_image_base64=None. This is fine to leave or reset by main agent/next tester.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Banner feature (4:1 crop + color swatches) fully verified working: backend persistence confirmed via curl, frontend UI/UX confirmed via Playwright with computed-style color verification. If retesting schedule-slot tests, first clean up times collection (07:00, 20:00 duplicates) or update test_backend.py to use unique/random time values per run to avoid pollution-caused failures.
rca_of_issue: Backend test failures were caused by test data pollution: times '07:00' and '20:00' were created in a previous testing iteration and never cleaned up (per test file's intentional no-cleanup policy). When test_backend.py re-ran, POST /api/times with the same duplicate time correctly returned 400 (expected validation behavior), but test code then tried to access ['id'] on the error response causing KeyError. This is a test script robustness issue, not an app defect - the duplicate-rejection business logic is working exactly as intended.
